## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the proper use, zeroing, taring, and routine
quality checks for the laboratory balances in the EA Program. Correct
weighing technique is fundamental to virtually every quantitative
laboratory procedure. For calibration and verification protocols, see
[SOP-L200 Analytical Balance Calibration](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All Mettler Toledo balances in the EA Program
  laboratory, including the basic balances (MS1602TS/00) and the
  precision balance (XPE205 DeltaRange)
- **Does not apply to:** Portable field balances or calibration
  procedures (see [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Dropping heavy items onto the balance pan can damage the
  weighing cell. Handle objects carefully and never exceed the rated
  capacity.
- **Chemical:** Some materials weighed on the balance may be hazardous.
  Refer to the relevant SOP for the material being weighed. Never place
  chemicals directly on the weighing pan; always use a sample vessel.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling chemical samples)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when weighing chemical reagents)

### Emergency Procedures

If a chemical spill occurs on or near the balance, clean the spill per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
before resuming use.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Specifications                            |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Basic Balance (3 units)       | Mettler Toledo MS1602TS/00; 1620 g max, d = 0.1 g |
| Precision Balance (1 unit)    | Mettler Toledo XPE205 DeltaRange; 81 g / 220 g max, d = 0.01 mg / 0.1 mg |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Weighing vessels (boats, beakers, etc.) | Appropriate to the material being weighed |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)    | For cleaning the weighing pan             |
| Forceps                       | For handling calibration weights (see [SOP-L25](SOP-L25-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd)) |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Switching On and Warm-Up

1. The balance switches on automatically when connected to the power
   supply
2. Before the balance gives reliable results, it must acclimatize to
   room temperature and warm up while connected to power. Refer to the
   instrument manual for the recommended warm-up time for each model.
3. To exit standby mode, press the power/standby key. The display turns
   on and the balance is ready immediately.

::: {.callout-note}
If the balance was completely disconnected from power for an extended
period, allow it to warm up for at least 30 minutes before use
[@harris2020].
:::

### 6.2 Zeroing the Balance

1. Open the draft shield (precision balance only)
2. Ensure the weighing pan is clear
3. Close the draft shield
4. Press the **Zero** key. The display reads 0.0000 g (precision) or
   0.0 g (basic)

### 6.3 Taring

If a sample vessel is used, tare the balance before adding sample
material:

1. Zero the balance (Section 6.2)
2. Open the draft shield
3. Place the sample vessel on the center of the weighing pan
4. Close the draft shield
5. Press the **Tare** key. The display reads zero and the **Net**
   indicator appears

### 6.4 Performing a Weighing

1. Open the draft shield (if applicable)
2. Place the weighing object into the tared sample vessel
3. Close the draft shield and wait for the stability indicator
4. Record the displayed mass in the lab notebook
5. If using the XPE205 electronic results feature, tap **Add result**
   to append the value to the results list

### 6.5 Completing and Saving Results (XPE205)

1. Tap **Complete** to open the task completion dialog
2. Select an option to save or print the results list
3. Follow the on-screen instructions
4. Tap **Complete** to finalize; the results list is saved or printed
   and then cleared

### 6.6 Shutdown

1. Remove all samples and vessels from the weighing pan
2. Clean the pan and draft shield interior with a lint-free wipe
3. Close the draft shield
4. To enter standby mode, hold the power/standby key. The display goes
   dark but the balance remains powered on and thermally stable.
5. To switch the balance off completely, disconnect from the power
   supply. Note that the balance will require a full warm-up before its
   next use.


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 Leveling the Balance

Exact horizontal positioning is essential for repeatable and accurate
results:

1. Check the spirit level before each use session
2. If the message "Balance is out of level" appears, tap **Level the
   balance** to open the leveling aid
3. Adjust the leveling feet following the on-screen instructions until
   the bubble is centered
4. The leveling aid can also be accessed via **Balance menu > Leveling
   aid**

### 7.2 Internal Adjustment (XPE205)

1. Navigate to **Methods > Adjustments**
2. Verify that the adjustment strategy is set to **Internal adjustment**
3. Open the Methods section, tap **Adjustments**, select the adjustment,
   and tap **Start** (or from the main weighing screen, tap **More >
   Start adjustment**)
4. Do not touch the balance during the adjustment
5. When complete, review the adjustment results
6. Tap **Print** if a record is needed, then tap **Finish adjustment**

For external calibration verification using traceable reference weights,
see [SOP-L25](SOP-L25-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd).


## 8. Waste Disposal

No waste is generated by this procedure. Cleaning materials (Kimwipes)
can be disposed of in standard trash unless they contacted hazardous
chemicals, in which case follow
[SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## 10. Training Record

Before using the laboratory balances independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L001 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L001-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate proper leveling, zeroing, taring, and weighing technique
   under supervision
4. For the XPE205 precision balance, also demonstrate use of the draft
   shield and internal adjustment procedure
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
